jobs.description:
Help shape the future of the next generation of leaders
UC Level 6, Salary Range $93,705 pa - $100,871 pa pro rata
+ 17% Super
3-day Part-Time Continuing Opportunity | Flexible Hours

About us:

Snow Scholarships have been co-created by Snow Foundation and the University of Canberra. Snow Foundation believes in the power of education to change lives and open doors - helping students realise their potential and grow into confident, purposeful leaders. In partnership with the University of Canberra, The Snow Foundation committed $20 million to back students who have big dreams and just need the support to get there.
University of Canberra’s vision is that “Together we work to empower, connect and share knowledge with our people, cultures and places.” UC is part of the fabric of the local community, and we aim to challenge the status quo through the pursuit of excellence in teaching, learning and research. The University of Canberra is deeply committed to reducing inequalities and making university accessible for students regardless of their background.
About the opportunity:

From the partnership between University of Canberra and the Snow Foundation, the Snow Scholarship is a new and transformative program, now in its first year, supporting students from diverse or Indigenous backgrounds from Canberra and regional or rural NSW who are facing barriers to higher education. The program provides support for the entire duration of their degree providing financial and pastoral care support, leadership development, First Nations experiences and education, and more. It’s about changing lives and creating impact, nurturing the next generation of leaders.
This is a great opportunity to join the Snow Scholarship team as the Snow Scholarship Program Coordinator and play a meaningful role in a groundbreaking scholarship program at the University of Canberra, helping change the lives of students and supporting them to achieve their potential.
Position Description: Snow Scholarship Program Coordinator.pdf

Key Responsibilities:

Coordinate the day-to-day administration and support delivery of the Snow Scholarship Program.
Build strong, trusted relationships with scholars and key stakeholders.
Provide empathetic, responsive, and high-quality support to students.
Coordinate program activities, communications, events, and key milestones. Occasional out-of-hours activity may be required for key events.
Identify opportunities to improve the scholar experience and strengthen program delivery.

About You:

You are dynamic, empathetic, and impact-driven, with a genuine passion for supporting students and helping them thrive. You bring strong experience in student support or program coordination, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to build trusted relationships with students and stakeholders.
This position is more than a job; it’s an opportunity to be part of a transformative program that changes lives.
Offerings/ Benefits/ Culture:

The University offers excellent conditions and benefits which can be explored on our “Work at UC” site which includes:
Flexible working arrangements and Family-friendly policies
On campus Gym, Medical services, Cafes, Post office, Supermarket and Early Childhood Education and Care facilities.
Professional Development offerings (study assistance, corporate programs and discounts)
Innovative work environment with a diverse and inclusive culture
Access to Employee Assistance Program and a corporate private Health Plan (Bupa)

University of Canberra embodies its Values of Everyone’s invites, Narragunnawali, Change the World, Dare to be Curious and Walk together which we are proud. UC sets a goal to be the national sector leader in equity, diversity, inclusion and access via Connected - A Decadal Strategy 2023-2032. UC encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.
What we need from you:
To be considered for this position, submit your application through the “Apply Now” tab with your CV and a cover letter outlining why you are a strong fit for this position.
If you are initially shortlisted, you may be asked to complete an online one-way video interview or a written assessment. There will be a list of pre-set questions that will need to be answered within a stipulated time.
Eligibility:

Applicants who wish to apply for this position must have valid working rights at the time of submission.
The University of Canberra is committed to the safety of vulnerable and young people. As such, the successful candidate will be required to have or obtain a current ACT working with vulnerable people registration.

please contact Claire Toepfer, Snow Scholarship Program Manager, claire.toepfer@canberra.edu.au.
For recruitment and application questions:
please contact the Talent Solutions team on 02 6206 3867 or email uctalent@canberra.edu.au. If you would like to request a reasonable adjustment to the selection process, please feel free to contact us.

jobs.title: Client Care Coordinator
jobs.description:
Client Care Coordinator

Senior Helpers of Baltimore and Central Maryland

Lutherville-Timonium, Maryland | Full-time | On-site with local travel
$50,000–$62,000 annually, based on experience, plus quarterly performance bonuses and benefits

Great home care starts long before a caregiver walks through the front door. It starts with listening, understanding what matters most, and helping a family feel confident about the next step.

We’re hiring a Client Care Coordinator who brings empathy, initiative, and strong relationship-building together into one meaningful role.

You’ll guide families from their first inquiry and assessment through enrollment and a successful start of care. Then you’ll own those relationships—staying connected, addressing concerns, and helping services evolve as needs change.

This role combines compassionate client service, consultative sales, and care coordination. Your ability to build trust and follow through will directly shape the client experience and our agency’s growth.

WHY JOIN US?
💜 The first and only home care agency in Maryland to earn CHAP Age-Friendly Care at Home Certification
💜 A team committed to raising the standard in home care
💜 A culture that believes great care starts with great people
💜 Meaningful ownership of client relationships, supported by experienced operations and nursing leadership

Our approach brings together the Age-Friendly 4Ms framework—What Matters, Medication, Mentation, and Mobility—with LIFE Profile assessments, Senior Gems dementia care, and hands-on caregiver training in our Center of Excellence.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Help families choose and begin care:
• Respond promptly to qualified inquiries and maintain consistent follow-up.
• Conduct non-clinical assessments, including Senior Helpers LIFE Profile assessments, in homes, facilities, and other approved settings.
• Understand client routines, preferences, support needs, family expectations, and urgency.
• Recommend appropriate services, schedules, and care hours.
• Explain service options, pricing, and agreements; address questions; and guide families toward informed enrollment decisions.
• Coordinate onboarding, caregiver introductions, and timely service starts.
Build relationships that last:
• Serve as the primary non-clinical relationship owner for an assigned portfolio of clients and families.
• Lead proactive calls, client visits, first-day and first-month follow-up, and satisfaction outreach.
• Complete assigned non-clinical reassessments and service-plan updates.
• Recognize concerns early, coordinate solutions, and follow through to resolution.
• Recommend service adjustments or additional support when changing needs and family goals warrant them.
• Reconnect with prospective and former clients when services may meet their needs.
Keep care coordinated:
• Partner with nursing, scheduling, caregivers, and business development to support responsive, consistent service.
• Coordinate service agreements, authorizations, payer-program documentation, and care transitions.
• Escalate clinical concerns, safety risks, and serious complaints to appropriate leadership.
• Maintain accurate client, assessment, service-plan, and pipeline records in WellSky.
• Support billing accuracy, quality assurance, and documentation compliance.
• Review conversion, satisfaction, retention, and service-utilization trends to recommend improvements.

WHAT YOU BRING

• One to three years of relevant experience preferred in home care, healthcare, senior services, admissions, care coordination, consultative sales, client services, or account management.
• Confidence assessing needs, explaining solutions, discussing pricing, and helping people make decisions.
• Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and follow-through.
• The ability to balance empathy with accountability for client experience and business results.
• Sound judgment and comfort managing competing priorities.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and comfort learning healthcare or client-management systems; WellSky experience is preferred.
• A valid driver’s license, current automobile insurance, reliable transportation, and availability for local travel.
• A bachelor’s degree in a related field is preferred.
Experience working with older adults and families is strongly preferred. Clinical assessments and decisions remain with appropriately licensed personnel.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Families receive timely, thoughtful guidance. Qualified inquiries become appropriate service starts. Clients feel heard and supported. Concerns are resolved, records stay current, and services evolve responsibly with each client’s needs.
You’ll report to the Director of Operations, with goals and priorities reviewed during your first 30, 60, and 90 days.

COMPENSATION & WORK ENVIRONMENT

• Annual base salary of $50,000–$62,000, based on experience.
• Quarterly performance bonuses.
• Benefits and PTO
• Full-time, based at our office at 1313 York Road in Lutherville-Timonium.
• Regular local travel throughout Baltimore and Central Maryland for assessments and client visits.
• Reasonable schedule flexibility to respond to prospective and active client needs.

If you want your work to matter—and want to help shape the future of aging care in Maryland—we’d love to meet you.
Senior Helpers is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to an inclusive, respectful, and professional workplace.

jobs.description:
Job Overview

University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is delighted to offer a fantastic opportunity to work with us.

Job Title: Administration Team Leader

Contract Type: Permanent

Under current Home Office rules, this role is not eligible for Skilled Worker visa sponsorship.

Please be advised that this vacancy may close earlier than stated if we receive a large number of applications.

Main duties of the job

This is an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Team Leader within our Clinic Support Team based in the Outpatient Administration Centre.

The role will require you to be responsible for overseeing our reception desks at Southampton General Hospital and assigning daily tasks to your team of Administrators and working towards deadline for patients to be seen.

We are looking for a pro-active, dynamic individual to work in this fast paced environment, who is able to be reactive to urgent requests from our stakeholders and work to extremely tight deadlines.

Someone who is highly innovative and self-motivated individual who will deliver a first class service to all of our patients.

Your duties will include;

Lead and manage a team of administrators, including recruitment, performance management, attendance, training, and annual appraisals.

Oversee and coordinate all administrative operations, including duty rosters, patient‑pathway processes, workload allocation, data accuracy, and compliance with policies and SOPs.

Ensure high‑quality, patient‑focused service delivery, including meeting national targets, resolving enquiries, managing confidential information, and escalating delays or issues impacting patient care.

Working for our organisation

As one of the largest acute teaching Trusts in England, we offer learning and development opportunities to help you achieve the career you aspire to. UHS is rated ‘Good’ by the CQC and in the latest national NHS Staff Survey, we were in the top 10 acute trusts for staff engagement and for staff recommending the hospital as a place to work or receive care.

We support flexible working and will consider requests taking into account the needs of the service. UHS employees are able to access a range of NHS discounts, are entitled to a minimum of 35 days paid holiday (pro rata), and we offer a generous pension scheme.

Southampton is an attractive place to live and work situated on the south coast, with an international airport and direct trains to London. The New Forest National Park and beaches of the Jurassic coast are also right on our doorstep. The city offers living costs 30% lower than London and 17 schools rated outstanding by Ofsted.

We believe that using technology wisely shows strong time management and commitment to innovation. However, personalising your recruitment application to highlight your unique skills and experiences is crucial. Relying too heavily on generic, AI-generated content instead of drawing from your own strengths and accomplishments may lead to your application being rejected if multiple candidates present identical or similar information.

leading and managing a team of administrators, including recruitment, performance management, attendance, training, and annual appraisals.

Manage resources and departmental support functions, such as authorising timesheets and orders and ensuring staff uphold customer service expectations.

jobs.description:
Your next possibility

Family Support Worker

£31,533.84 - £35,764.36 Annually (Actual)

Birmingham

B23 5AJFull Time

SW

Story Wood School

About The Role

About this Role

Core Purpose

Story Wood is looking for an exceptional Family Support Worker that promotes the safety, well-being and inclusion of all pupils.

The post-holder will take daily operational responsibility for safeguarding, attendance and behaviour, working closely with the Deputy Headteacher (Pastoral lead/DSL) and SENCO to ensure that every child is safe, supported and ready to learn. This role is central to building strong relationships with families, removing barriers to learning, and supporting pupils with complex needs, including those with SEND.

The post-holder will take daily operational responsibility for safeguarding, attendance and behaviour, working closely with the Deputy Headteacher (Pastoral lead/DSL) and SENCO to ensure that every child is safe, supported and ready to learn.

This role is central to building strong relationships with families, removing barriers to learning, and supporting pupils with complex needs, including those with SEND.

Key Responsibilities

Safeguarding and Pupil Wellbeing

Serving as a Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL), ensuring that safeguarding systems and procedures are robust and effective.

Manage and respond to day-to-day safeguarding concerns, maintaining accurate records and following school policy.

Support the DSL and Senior Mental Health Lead in coordinating early help and intervention for pupils and families in need.

Work collaboratively with outside agencies (e.g. Social Care, Early Help, CAMHS, Police) to secure the best outcomes for pupils.

Provide emotional support and guidance for pupils, modelling restorative and trauma-informed approaches.

Attendance and Family Engagement

Lead on improving attendance and punctuality through effective monitoring, analysis and communication with families.

Carry out home visits where necessary to engage with parents and carers, addressing barriers to regular attendance.

Work with the Deputy Headteacher and admin staff to develop and implement attendance improvement strategies.

Celebrate good attendance and promote positive attitudes towards school.

Behaviour and Inclusion

Support staff in implementing the school’s Behaviour and Expectations Policy, ensuring a consistent and positive approach Provide direct support for pupils with behavioural and emotional needs, particularly those with complex circumstances.

Lead or contribute to individual behaviour plans, risk assessments and reintegration programmes.

Promote restorative practices and support staff in managing challenging behaviour constructively.

Planning and running structured lunchtime Nurture Groups and afternoon mentoring sessions (group and 1:1) focused on emotional regulation, self-esteem, trauma recovery, and social skills.

Support for SEND and Inclusion

Work closely with the SENCO to ensure that pupils with SEND or additional needs receive appropriate support.

Assist with coordinating interventions, monitoring provision and communicating with families of pupils with SEND.

Contribute to review meetings and liaise with external professionals involved in SEND support.

Support teachers and support staff in developing inclusive classroom strategies that meet pupils’ diverse needs.

In the event of staff changes, the post-holder may be required to take on temporary SENCO, class teacher responsibilities, with guidance and professional development provided by the school.

Professional Conduct and Collaboration

Uphold the highest standards of professionalism, confidentiality and integrity.

Build positive and trusting relationships with pupils, families and colleagues.

Work collaboratively with the Deputy Headteacher, SENCO, DSLs and other leaders to drive school improvement in inclusion and pastoral care.

Contribute to staff training and professional development in areas of safeguarding, behaviour and inclusion.

Represent the school at external meetings, panels and multi-agency forums when required.

We Are Looking For Someone Who

Is genuinely passionate about improving life outcomes for vulnerable children and hard-to-reach families in a community-centered primary school.
Is highly proactive, self-motivated, and comfortable working directly with both children in school and parents in the community.
Has proven experience in delivering direct pupil interventions (such as Nurture Groups or 1:1 emotional regulation mentoring).
Understands Early Help frameworks, safeguarding systems, and multi-agency working.
Can balance high compassion with high expectations, holding parents accountable while offering practical, relational support.
Demonstrates exceptional professional integrity, resilience, and organisational skills.
Is eager to engage in continuous professional development and committed to applying evidence-informed research and strategies to support families, remove barriers to learning, and nurture pupil well-being.

Person Specification

Essential

Experience working with vulnerable children and families in a pastoral or safeguarding capacity. Or skills which are transferrable to this role.
Strong understanding of safeguarding, attendance and behaviour management procedures.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trust quickly.
Confidence in managing sensitive conversations and challenging situations.
Experience of working with external agencies and multi-agency plans.
Commitment to inclusion and improving life chances for all pupils.

Desirable

Experience of working alongside or supporting a SENCO.
Working knowledge of the SEND Code of Practice (2015).
Relevant qualifications in safeguarding, counselling, behaviour, or inclusion.
Experience of leading attendance or behaviour initiatives.

How to Apply and School Visits

We strongly encourage prospective candidates to visit our school and experience our culture first-hand before applying. To arrange a visit or request an application pack, please contact the school office on 0121 464 3863 or email enquiries@storywoodschool.co.uk.

Closing Date: 12:00 Monday 21st September 2026

Interviews: TBC

jobs.title: After Hours Care Coordinator (Remote | Part-Time)
jobs.description:
The After-Hours Coordinator serves as the main point of contact for clients, caregivers, and staff outside of regular business hours. This role is responsible for responding to urgent calls, coordinating caregiver coverage for call-outs and schedule changes, addressing client concerns, documenting incidents, and helping ensure there are no interruptions in care.

The After-Hours Coordinator works closely with the care team to address issues quickly, maintain quality of service, and provide support to both clients and caregivers during evenings, weekends, and holidays.

After-Hours Schedule

Monday–Friday:
4:30 PM – 8:00 AM the following morning

Weekend Coverage:
Weekend coverage is required every weekend on a rotating schedule. Coordinators alternate between Saturday and Sunday coverage each week.

One weekend: Saturday, 8:00 AM – 8:00 AM Sunday
Following weekend: Sunday, 8:00 AM – 8:00 AM Monday

This rotation allows for consistent after-hours coverage while sharing weekend responsibilities among the team.

Typical After-Hours Calls

Calls are primarily related to urgent staffing and client care needs that occur outside of normal business hours.

Typical calls may include:

Caregiver call-outs due to illness, emergencies, transportation issues, or other unexpected absences
Schedule changes requested by clients, families, or caregivers
Finding replacement caregivers when a scheduled caregiver is unable to work
Client concerns or complaints that require immediate attention
Caregiver questions regarding client care plans, shift details, or emergency procedures
Emergency situations involving client health or safety, including hospitalizations, falls, or situations requiring emergency services
Late arrivals or no-shows reported by clients or caregivers
Hospital admissions or discharges that require updates to the care schedule
Requests for additional services or visits outside of the regular schedule

The majority of after-hours calls are related to caregiver call-outs, finding coverage, schedule adjustments, and client concerns that need an immediate response. This role is essential to helping ensure uninterrupted care and maintaining a positive experience for our clients and caregivers.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for someone who is:

Highly organized and dependable
Comfortable multitasking and managing multiple priorities
Able to stay calm and professional in a fast-paced environment
Strong at problem-solving and communication
Comfortable making decisions and handling urgent situations
Responsive and reliable during scheduled after-hours coverage

Compensation

$18/hour + on-call stipend: $40 per weekday and $50 per weekend day.

We’re looking for someone who is highly organized, dependable, able to multitask effectively, and skilled at prioritizing responsibilities in a fast-paced environment. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you!

new_jobs.description:
Client Care Coordinator

Senior Helpers of Baltimore and Central Maryland

Lutherville-Timonium, Maryland | Full-time | On-site with local travel
$50,000–$62,000 annually, based on experience, plus quarterly performance bonuses and benefits

Great home care starts long before a caregiver walks through the front door. It starts with listening, understanding what matters most, and helping a family feel confident about the next step.

We’re hiring a Client Care Coordinator who brings empathy, initiative, and strong relationship-building together into one meaningful role.

You’ll guide families from their first inquiry and assessment through enrollment and a successful start of care. Then you’ll own those relationships—staying connected, addressing concerns, and helping services evolve as needs change.

This role combines compassionate client service, consultative sales, and care coordination. Your ability to build trust and follow through will directly shape the client experience and our agency’s growth.

WHY JOIN US?
💜 The first and only home care agency in Maryland to earn CHAP Age-Friendly Care at Home Certification
💜 A team committed to raising the standard in home care
💜 A culture that believes great care starts with great people
💜 Meaningful ownership of client relationships, supported by experienced operations and nursing leadership

Our approach brings together the Age-Friendly 4Ms framework—What Matters, Medication, Mentation, and Mobility—with LIFE Profile assessments, Senior Gems dementia care, and hands-on caregiver training in our Center of Excellence.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Help families choose and begin care:
• Respond promptly to qualified inquiries and maintain consistent follow-up.
• Conduct non-clinical assessments, including Senior Helpers LIFE Profile assessments, in homes, facilities, and other approved settings.
• Understand client routines, preferences, support needs, family expectations, and urgency.
• Recommend appropriate services, schedules, and care hours.
• Explain service options, pricing, and agreements; address questions; and guide families toward informed enrollment decisions.
• Coordinate onboarding, caregiver introductions, and timely service starts.
Build relationships that last:
• Serve as the primary non-clinical relationship owner for an assigned portfolio of clients and families.
• Lead proactive calls, client visits, first-day and first-month follow-up, and satisfaction outreach.
• Complete assigned non-clinical reassessments and service-plan updates.
• Recognize concerns early, coordinate solutions, and follow through to resolution.
• Recommend service adjustments or additional support when changing needs and family goals warrant them.
• Reconnect with prospective and former clients when services may meet their needs.
Keep care coordinated:
• Partner with nursing, scheduling, caregivers, and business development to support responsive, consistent service.
• Coordinate service agreements, authorizations, payer-program documentation, and care transitions.
• Escalate clinical concerns, safety risks, and serious complaints to appropriate leadership.
• Maintain accurate client, assessment, service-plan, and pipeline records in WellSky.
• Support billing accuracy, quality assurance, and documentation compliance.
• Review conversion, satisfaction, retention, and service-utilization trends to recommend improvements.

WHAT YOU BRING

• One to three years of relevant experience preferred in home care, healthcare, senior services, admissions, care coordination, consultative sales, client services, or account management.
• Confidence assessing needs, explaining solutions, discussing pricing, and helping people make decisions.
• Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and follow-through.
• The ability to balance empathy with accountability for client experience and business results.
• Sound judgment and comfort managing competing priorities.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and comfort learning healthcare or client-management systems; WellSky experience is preferred.
• A valid driver’s license, current automobile insurance, reliable transportation, and availability for local travel.
• A bachelor’s degree in a related field is preferred.
Experience working with older adults and families is strongly preferred. Clinical assessments and decisions remain with appropriately licensed personnel.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Families receive timely, thoughtful guidance. Qualified inquiries become appropriate service starts. Clients feel heard and supported. Concerns are resolved, records stay current, and services evolve responsibly with each client’s needs.
You’ll report to the Director of Operations, with goals and priorities reviewed during your first 30, 60, and 90 days.

COMPENSATION & WORK ENVIRONMENT

• Annual base salary of $50,000–$62,000, based on experience.
• Quarterly performance bonuses.
• Benefits and PTO
• Full-time, based at our office at 1313 York Road in Lutherville-Timonium.
• Regular local travel throughout Baltimore and Central Maryland for assessments and client visits.
• Reasonable schedule flexibility to respond to prospective and active client needs.

If you want your work to matter—and want to help shape the future of aging care in Maryland—we’d love to meet you.
Senior Helpers is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to an inclusive, respectful, and professional workplace.

About this Role

Core Purpose

Story Wood is looking for an exceptional Family Support Worker that promotes the safety, well-being and inclusion of all pupils.

The post-holder will take daily operational responsibility for safeguarding, attendance and behaviour, working closely with the Deputy Headteacher (Pastoral lead/DSL) and SENCO to ensure that every child is safe, supported and ready to learn. This role is central to building strong relationships with families, removing barriers to learning, and supporting pupils with complex needs, including those with SEND.

The post-holder will take daily operational responsibility for safeguarding, attendance and behaviour, working closely with the Deputy Headteacher (Pastoral lead/DSL) and SENCO to ensure that every child is safe, supported and ready to learn.

This role is central to building strong relationships with families, removing barriers to learning, and supporting pupils with complex needs, including those with SEND.

Key Responsibilities

Safeguarding and Pupil Wellbeing

Serving as a Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL), ensuring that safeguarding systems and procedures are robust and effective.

Manage and respond to day-to-day safeguarding concerns, maintaining accurate records and following school policy.

Support the DSL and Senior Mental Health Lead in coordinating early help and intervention for pupils and families in need.

Work collaboratively with outside agencies (e.g. Social Care, Early Help, CAMHS, Police) to secure the best outcomes for pupils.

Provide emotional support and guidance for pupils, modelling restorative and trauma-informed approaches.

Attendance and Family Engagement

Lead on improving attendance and punctuality through effective monitoring, analysis and communication with families.

Carry out home visits where necessary to engage with parents and carers, addressing barriers to regular attendance.

Work with the Deputy Headteacher and admin staff to develop and implement attendance improvement strategies.

Celebrate good attendance and promote positive attitudes towards school.

Behaviour and Inclusion

Support staff in implementing the school’s Behaviour and Expectations Policy, ensuring a consistent and positive approach Provide direct support for pupils with behavioural and emotional needs, particularly those with complex circumstances.

Lead or contribute to individual behaviour plans, risk assessments and reintegration programmes.

Promote restorative practices and support staff in managing challenging behaviour constructively.

Planning and running structured lunchtime Nurture Groups and afternoon mentoring sessions (group and 1:1) focused on emotional regulation, self-esteem, trauma recovery, and social skills.

Support for SEND and Inclusion

Work closely with the SENCO to ensure that pupils with SEND or additional needs receive appropriate support.

Assist with coordinating interventions, monitoring provision and communicating with families of pupils with SEND.

Contribute to review meetings and liaise with external professionals involved in SEND support.

Support teachers and support staff in developing inclusive classroom strategies that meet pupils’ diverse needs.

In the event of staff changes, the post-holder may be required to take on temporary SENCO, class teacher responsibilities, with guidance and professional development provided by the school.

Professional Conduct and Collaboration

Uphold the highest standards of professionalism, confidentiality and integrity.

Build positive and trusting relationships with pupils, families and colleagues.

Work collaboratively with the Deputy Headteacher, SENCO, DSLs and other leaders to drive school improvement in inclusion and pastoral care.

Contribute to staff training and professional development in areas of safeguarding, behaviour and inclusion.

Represent the school at external meetings, panels and multi-agency forums when required.

We Are Looking For Someone Who

Is genuinely passionate about improving life outcomes for vulnerable children and hard-to-reach families in a community-centered primary school.
Is highly proactive, self-motivated, and comfortable working directly with both children in school and parents in the community.
Has proven experience in delivering direct pupil interventions (such as Nurture Groups or 1:1 emotional regulation mentoring).
Understands Early Help frameworks, safeguarding systems, and multi-agency working.
Can balance high compassion with high expectations, holding parents accountable while offering practical, relational support.
Demonstrates exceptional professional integrity, resilience, and organisational skills.
Is eager to engage in continuous professional development and committed to applying evidence-informed research and strategies to support families, remove barriers to learning, and nurture pupil well-being.

Person Specification

Essential

Experience working with vulnerable children and families in a pastoral or safeguarding capacity. Or skills which are transferrable to this role.
Strong understanding of safeguarding, attendance and behaviour management procedures.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trust quickly.
Confidence in managing sensitive conversations and challenging situations.
Experience of working with external agencies and multi-agency plans.
Commitment to inclusion and improving life chances for all pupils.

Desirable

Experience of working alongside or supporting a SENCO.
Working knowledge of the SEND Code of Practice (2015).
Relevant qualifications in safeguarding, counselling, behaviour, or inclusion.
Experience of leading attendance or behaviour initiatives.

We strongly encourage prospective candidates to visit our school and experience our culture first-hand before applying. To arrange a visit or request an application pack, please contact the school office on 0121 464 3863 or email enquiries@storywoodschool.co.uk.

The After-Hours Coordinator serves as the main point of contact for clients, caregivers, and staff outside of regular business hours. This role is responsible for responding to urgent calls, coordinating caregiver coverage for call-outs and schedule changes, addressing client concerns, documenting incidents, and helping ensure there are no interruptions in care.

The After-Hours Coordinator works closely with the care team to address issues quickly, maintain quality of service, and provide support to both clients and caregivers during evenings, weekends, and holidays.

After-Hours Schedule

Monday–Friday:
4:30 PM – 8:00 AM the following morning

Weekend Coverage:
Weekend coverage is required every weekend on a rotating schedule. Coordinators alternate between Saturday and Sunday coverage each week.

One weekend: Saturday, 8:00 AM – 8:00 AM Sunday
Following weekend: Sunday, 8:00 AM – 8:00 AM Monday

This rotation allows for consistent after-hours coverage while sharing weekend responsibilities among the team.

Typical After-Hours Calls

Calls are primarily related to urgent staffing and client care needs that occur outside of normal business hours.

Typical calls may include:

Caregiver call-outs due to illness, emergencies, transportation issues, or other unexpected absences
Schedule changes requested by clients, families, or caregivers
Finding replacement caregivers when a scheduled caregiver is unable to work
Client concerns or complaints that require immediate attention
Caregiver questions regarding client care plans, shift details, or emergency procedures
Emergency situations involving client health or safety, including hospitalizations, falls, or situations requiring emergency services
Late arrivals or no-shows reported by clients or caregivers
Hospital admissions or discharges that require updates to the care schedule
Requests for additional services or visits outside of the regular schedule

The majority of after-hours calls are related to caregiver call-outs, finding coverage, schedule adjustments, and client concerns that need an immediate response. This role is essential to helping ensure uninterrupted care and maintaining a positive experience for our clients and caregivers.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for someone who is:

Highly organized and dependable
Comfortable multitasking and managing multiple priorities
Able to stay calm and professional in a fast-paced environment
Strong at problem-solving and communication
Comfortable making decisions and handling urgent situations
Responsive and reliable during scheduled after-hours coverage

Compensation

$18/hour + on-call stipend: $40 per weekday and $50 per weekend day.

We’re looking for someone who is highly organized, dependable, able to multitask effectively, and skilled at prioritizing responsibilities in a fast-paced environment. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you!
